label: <DEL> in short sequences, plus early w/g/z inputs
explanation: Two components, both confined to roughly absolute steps 2-6. (1) The <DEL> step, which holds about 59% of activation mass. It fires much more in short sequences: 75% of <DEL> steps are active when L<=5, and it fades for L>=7. (2) Original-phase inputs of particular letters: w is the strongest (6x lift, and the top activations are a second or third w in a row), then g and z, with weaker contributions from e and t. These mostly fire at t=2..6 and on the first occurrence of the token (in_first carries 92% of mass). It essentially never fires in the copy phase (14 of 546k steps), never at t=0, and almost never on digits or on letters like c, u, b, j. The predicate gets F1 0.67 and mass recall 0.89 on dev. Misses are mostly weak activations on e/t, and on <DEL> right after a w/g/z in longer sequences. False positives are w/g/z that come after other tokens and <DEL> steps at L=6 that stay below threshold, so magnitude seems to depend on recent context that this predicate does not capture.
